title: Patient Payment Plan Fee Schedule
content:
Patient Payment Plan agreements carry no interest; the only plan fees are the late fee for a missed installment and the returned-payment fee for a payment that comes back unpaid. The schedule below gives each tier's figures.

| Tier | Grace period after the due date (calendar days) | Late fee (USD) | Most late fees over the life of one plan | First late fee waived on the patient's request | Returned-payment fee (USD) | A declined card also incurs the returned-payment fee |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Short-Term 3-Month Payment Plan | 10 | 10.00 | 3 | Yes | 25.00 | No |
| Standard 6-Month Payment Plan | 10 | 10.00 | 3 | Yes | 25.00 | No |
| Extended 10-Month Payment Plan | 10 | 10.00 | 3 | Yes | 25.00 | No |
| Long-Term 12-Month Payment Plan | 10 | 10.00 | 3 | Yes | 25.00 | No |
| Large-Balance 18-Month Payment Plan | 10 | 10.00 | 3 | Yes | 25.00 | No |
| Hardship 24-Month Payment Plan | 15 | 0.00 | 0 | No | 0.00 | No |

Footnotes to the schedule:

1. The grace period is counted in calendar days after an installment's due date; an installment still unpaid at its end counts as missed. It is 10 calendar days on five tiers and 15 on the Hardship 24-Month Payment Plan.
2. A figure of 0.00 means the tier has no such fee. The Hardship 24-Month Payment Plan carries neither a late fee nor a returned-payment fee, and its limit on late fees is 0.
3. No tier applies the returned-payment fee to a declined card.
